334235.title: The semilinear reducibility conjecture for zigzag graph completions
334235.statement:
Let $ZZ_h$ be the zigzag graph with $h=h_G\geq 3$ loops, and let $\widehat{ZZ}_h$ be its completion. The notation $c_2(\widehat{ZZ}_h)_q$ denotes the $c_2$ invariant over a finite field of cardinality $q$.

**Semilinear reducibility conjecture.** For every $h\geq 3$, the graph $\widehat{ZZ}_h$ is semilinearly reducible and, for every $q$ with no primes of bad reduction,

$$
c_2(\widehat{ZZ}_h)_q\equiv -h_G(h_G+2)\pmod q.
$$

The conjecture concerns the same zigzag-completion assertion as the formula stated elsewhere in the paper: the formula is verified in the paper for $h\leq 8$, while the all-$h$ claim remains open.
334235.source_labels: v1 Conjecture 25; published Conjecture 20 and Proposition 21
334235.analysis: Source conjectures semilinear reducibility of completed zigzags and c2=-h(h+2) modulo every prime power, without bad primes. The source verifies h=3..8. Published PDF retains the conjecture. A finite point count does not establish semilinear reducibility. No source-formula evaluation is offered as discovery.
334235.remaining_gap: Produce uniform Dodgson-polynomial reduction beyond h=8, with literal reduction semantics; no such recurrence proved.

334318.title: Jaeger–Linial–Payan–Tarsi conjecture on _3-connected graphs
334318.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite graph without loops, possibly with multiple edges. A graph is **$\mathbb{Z}_3$-connected** if, for every zero-sum function $\beta:V(G)\to\mathbb{Z}_3$, there is an orientation $D$ such that

$$
d_D^+(v)-d_D^-(v)=\beta(v)\pmod 3
$$

for every vertex $v\in V(G)$. **Jaeger, Linial, Payan and Tarsi's conjecture.** Every $5$-edge-connected graph is $\mathbb{Z}_3$-connected. This generalizes the relationship between nowhere-zero flows and modulo orientations; it remains open, while every $6$-edge-connected graph is known to be $\mathbb{Z}_3$-connected.
334318.analysis: 5-edge-connected loopless multigraphs must realize every zero-sum Z3 boundary by an orientation; 6-edge-connected case is already known. Small-order simple graph diagnostics do not cover multigraphs or prove the conjecture.
334318.remaining_gap: Need new full-scope 5-edge-connectivity argument or a certified missing boundary on a 5-edge-connected graph.

334453.title: Local constraints imply bounded extrema
334453.statement:
Let $d\ge 3$ be an integer and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finite list of graphs. Let $\mathcal{G}_d(\mathcal{F})$ be the set of finite $d$-regular graphs that do not contain any element of $\mathcal{F}$ as an induced subgraph. Write $i(G)$ for the number of independent sets of $G$ and $v(G)$ for its number of vertices. **Local constraints imply bounded extrema.** There exist $G_{\min},G_{\max}\in\mathcal{G}_d(\mathcal{F})$ such that for every $G\in\mathcal{G}_d(\mathcal{F})$,

$$
i(G_{\min})^{1/v(G_{\min})}\le i(G)^{1/v(G)}\le i(G_{\max})^{1/v(G_{\max})}.
$$

This conjecture proposes that both extrema in the finite-degree local-constraint problem are attained by finite graphs. The general problem is described as very much open.
334453.source_labels: v2 Conjecture 9.6; author-hosted published Monthly pages
334453.analysis: For every fixed degree and finite forbidden-induced-subgraph list, finite extrema are conjectured. Choosing forbidden lists with empty admissible class would only give an excluded formulation correction. A finite sweep cannot disprove attainment over an unbounded class. No infinite strict-improvement family proved.
334453.remaining_gap: Exhibit a nonempty hereditary regular class and prove its extremal independent-set rate is not attained, or prove finite attainment. No finite experiment claimed.

334519.title: (4,6)-cage occupancy-fraction conjecture
334519.statement:
Let $\alpha_G(\lambda)$ denote the occupancy fraction of a graph $G$ in the hard-core model, and let $H_{4,6}$ be the $(4,6)$-cage. **(4,6)-cage occupancy-fraction conjecture.** For every $4$-regular graph $G$ of girth at least $5$ and every $\lambda>0$,

$$
\alpha_G(\lambda)\leq\alpha_{H_{4,6}}(\lambda).
$$

This is the proposed $4$-regular analogue of the corresponding extremal result and remains open.
334519.analysis: Later primary theorem explicitly gives a 4-regular graph G32 of girth at least 5 with occupancy fraction larger than that of H4,6 for every fugacity greater than 37. This exactly refutes the target. The later paper proof compares the two independence polynomials; no new search justified. Published Math. Comp. 95 (2026), 2091-2102, DOI 10.1090/mcom/4121.

334564.title: Large matching with bounded representation conjecture
334564.statement:
For every positive integer $m$, let $c(m)$ be a number. Let $G$ be a bipartite graph and let $E_1,\ldots,E_m$ be arbitrary edge sets. **Bounded representation conjecture.** There exists a matching $S$ in $G$ such that

$$
|S|\geqslant\frac{|E(G)|}{\Delta(G)}-c(m),
$$

and

$$
|S\cap E_i|\leqslant\left\lceil\frac{|E_i|}{\Delta(G)}\right\rceil\quad\text{for all }i\leqslant m.
$$

The conjecture reframes the preceding fair-representation questions as under-representation by a large matching; the source gives no resolution.
334564.analysis: c(m) is existential and depends only on m. All 262144 ordered pairs of arbitrary edge sets of K3,3 admit a full perfect matching meeting both ceil(|Ei|/3) upper quotas. Thus this bounded case has deficit zero. This cannot refute or prove existence of a uniform c(m). The source conjectures even c(m)=m/2 might suffice.
334564.remaining_gap: Need rounding of the uniform fractional matching with bounded additive loss depending only on m, independent of order and maximum degree. A fixed-instance positive deficit is insufficient.

334569.title: The degree conjecture for subgroup-counting polynomials of finite abelian p-groups
334569.statement: Let $p$ be prime and let $N(p^a,p^b,p^c,p^d)$ denote the polynomial counting subgroups of the finite abelian group $\mathbb{Z}_{p^a}\times\mathbb{Z}_{p^b}\times\mathbb{Z}_{p^c}\times\mathbb{Z}_{p^d}$, where $1\le a\le b\le c\le d$. **Degree conjecture.** For every $1\le a\le b\le c\le d$, the degree of $N(p^a,p^b,p^c,p^d)$ is $2a+b+c$. 334829.title: Nonexistence conjecture for balanced neighborly homology spheres with 6k vertices
334829.statement: Let $k\geq 2$. A **balanced $k$-neighborly homology $(2k-1)$-sphere** is a balanced simplicial homology sphere of dimension $2k-1$ in which every set of at most $k$ vertices with distinct colors is a face. **Nonexistence conjecture.** For an arbitrary $k\geq 2$, there does not exist a balanced $k$-neighborly homology $(2k-1)$-sphere with $6k$ vertices. This conjecture concerns the first non-trivial case in the proposed existence problem for balanced $k$-neighborly homology $(2k-1)$-spheres with equally sized color classes; its status is not resolved in the source.

334889.title: Quadratic zero-sum block conjecture for two-valued sequences
334889.statement:
Let $r$, $s$ and $k$ be positive integers such that $(r+s)$ divides $k$. A function $f:[n]\to\{-r,s\}$ has total sum $f([n])=0$ when the sum of its values over $[n]$ is zero. A **ZS $k$-block** is a set of $k$ consecutive integers whose $f$-sum is zero. **Quadratic zero-sum block conjecture.** There exists a constant $c(r,s)$ such that, if

$$
n\geq \frac{rs}{(r+s)^2}k^2+c(r,s)k,
$$

then every function $f:[n]\to\{-r,s\}$ with $f([n])=0$ contains a ZS $k$-block. This conjecture would extend the paper's zero-sum block theorem from the values $\{-1,1\}$ to arbitrary positive integers $r$ and $s$; the authors indicate that it should be provable by similar methods, but leave it open.
334889.analysis: Sun determines the exact threshold N(r,s,k), explicitly resolving the source conjecture. The theorem handles coprime r<s; division by gcd and swapping/negating covers the remaining unequal cases, while the equal case is the original +/-1 result. JCTA 179 (2021), 105385. No new threshold proof attempted.

334926.title: Simultaneous deficit conjecture for independent sets of paths
334926.statement:
Let $P$ be a path with vertex set $V$, and let $(A_1,\ldots,A_m)$ be a partition of $V$. **Simultaneous deficit conjecture.** There exists a subset $S\subseteq V$ independent in $P$ such that

$$
|S\cap A_i|\ge \frac{|A_i|}{2}-1
$$

for every $i\le m$, with strict inequality holding for all but at most $m/2$ of the sets $A_i$. The claim strengthens the separately known total-deficit and almost-fair representation bounds for paths. The supplied text gives no resolution status.
334926.analysis: The later theorem gives two disjoint independent sets covering all but one vertex in each color class, each satisfying |Si intersect Vj| >= |Vj|/2-1. Their total intersection size |Vj|-1 implies one of the two is strict on at least half of the classes. This is exactly the conjecture, including odd m by integrality. Later published EJC 24(3) P3.41, DOI 10.37236/7079, PDF retrieved.
334926.remaining_gap: No new result; prior proof body uses octahedral Tucker labeling.

373247.title: Chromatic-index conjecture for signed complete graphs of even order
373247.statement:
Let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n$ vertices, let $\sigma$ be a signature on $K_n$, and let $\chi ' (K_n, \sigma)$ denote its signed chromatic index. **Chromatic-index conjecture.** If $n \geq 8$ is even, then

$$
\chi ' (K_n, \sigma) = n-1.
$$

The paper establishes the analogous signature-independent value for even orders $n=4$ and $n=6$; the asserted formula for all even $n\geq 8$ remains open based on the supplied text.
373247.analysis: Use the source incidence-color convention: gamma(v,e)=-sigma(e)gamma(w,e), distinct colors at each vertex, palette 0,+/-1,...,+/-(n-2)/2. Normalize a star by switching. A perfect matching receives zero; positive-sign-product cycles in remaining spanning 2-factors receive +/- color pairs. Exhaustive K8 normalized signatures all pass a round-robin-pair template; 700 sampled signatures each at n=10,12,14,16 also pass. This is finite evidence only. The MathDB additional reference 1610.01676 actually retrieves Coloring Decompositions of Complete Geometric Graphs, not this signed-graph claim; not used as support.
373247.remaining_gap: Need balanced 2-factorization after deleting an appropriate perfect matching for every signature and every even order, or a literal non-colorability certificate. No universal theorem proved.

329603.title: First-elongation characterization for uniformly coloured spherical frameworks
329603.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a graph with a uniform vertex-colouring $chi$, and let ${\cal R}_d(V)$ denote the rigidity matroid in dimension $d$. A framework $(G,\chi)$ is isostatic on the sphere $r\mathbb{S}^d$ when it is rigid and has no redundant edges.

**First-elongation conjecture.** Suppose $(G=(V,E),\chi)$ is uniformly coloured. Then $(G,\chi)$ is isostatic on $r\mathbb{S}^d$ if and only if $G$ is simple and $E$ is a base of the first elongation of ${\cal R}_d(V)$.

This gives a proposed exact matroidal characterization of uniformly coloured isostatic frameworks in arbitrary dimension. The supplied text provides no resolution.
329603.analysis: The intended setting is generic uniformly expanding spherical frameworks. Dimensions at most 2 follow from the source theorems. The source isolates the higher-dimensional gap: a nonzero stress on a generic rigid spherical circuit must have nonzero sum of vertex stresses. Degenerate realizations and already-solved low dimensions cannot qualify. No generic symbolic rank calculation completed.
329603.remaining_gap: Prove the nonzero stress-sum lemma in d>=3 or exhibit a generic circuit where it vanishes identically; rational specializations alone do not prove generic failure.

329855.title: The existence conjecture for difference covering arrays satisfying P1 and P2
329855.statement: Let $p$ be a positive integer with $p\geq 3$. 329942.title: Non-power cardinality conjecture for modular $p$-free sets
329942.statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime. A set is **modular $p$-free** if it is modular and contains no nontrivial arithmetic progression of length $p$; $|A|$ denotes its cardinality.

**Non-power cardinality conjecture.** For every $n\in\mathbb{N}\cup\{0\}$, there exists a modular $p$-free set $A$ such that

$$
|A|\ne (p-1)^n.
$$

The paper states that the only resolved case is $p=3$, with examples supplied there; the general assertion is therefore open.
329942.analysis: Source literal quantifier for every n exists A with |A| != (p-1)^n is weaker than its discussion of one cardinality outside all powers; trivial varying witnesses would be zero-credit wording work. Search targets the substantive discussion, using distinct-residue modular p-AP freeness and strictly increasing first p-1 residues for coverage. Source example S5(0,3) modulo 25 passes an independent convention sanity check. Completed p=5 searches N=11,17,23,25,49 and p=7,N=49 find no nonpower set. N=75,p=5 was killed at wall limit, no completion or coverage claim.
329942.remaining_gap: Need a uniform construction over odd primes of modular sets outside all powers. A fixed-prime example alone would not resolve all-prime scope; composite-modulus repeated-residue conventions require fidelity review.

329971.title: The bounded-degree graph conjecture for Bernoulli CMP
329971.statement: Let $G$ be an infinite graph with bounded degrees. 330095.title: Haase's face-subgroup conjecture for permutation polytopes
330095.statement:
Let $G\leq S_n$ be a subgroup, and let $P(G)$ be the convex hull of the permutation matrices in $G$. For a subgroup $H\leq G$, write $P(H)\preceq P(G)$ when $P(H)$ is a face of $P(G)$. For a partition $[n]=\bigsqcup I_k$, define

$$
\operatorname{stab}(G;(I_k)_k):=\{\sigma\in G:\sigma(I_k)=I_k\text{ for all }k\}.
$$

**Haase's face-subgroup conjecture.** If $H\leq G$ and $P(H)\preceq P(G)$ is a face, then there is a partition

$$
[n]=\bigsqcup I_k
$$

such that

$$
H=\operatorname{stab}(G;(I_k)_k).
$$

The conjecture characterizes the subgroups whose permutation polytopes occur as faces of $P(G)$, extending the fact that stabilizers of partitions always yield faces. Its resolution status is not specified in the supplied source material.
330095.analysis: The same one-page source explicitly proves Conjecture 2. Average permutation matrices depend only on orbit partitions; H and its orbit-partition stabilizer yield faces with a common relative interior point, hence equal faces and equal vertex groups. No discovery credit for formalizing that proof.

330160.title: Ding's conjectured difference sets from trinomials
330160.statement:
Let $m\geq 5$ be odd. For $f\in\operatorname{GF}(2^m)[x]$, define

$$
D_f=\{f(x):x\in\operatorname{GF}(2^m)\}\setminus\{0\}.
$$

The listed eleven trinomials $f$ are the polynomials specified in the source statement. **Ding's difference-set conjecture.** For every one of those trinomials, $D_f$ is a difference set in $(\operatorname{GF}(2^m)^*,\times)$ with Singer parameters

$$
(2^m,\,2^{m-1},\,2^{m-2}).
$$

These are conjectured cyclic difference sets intended to produce binary linear codes; the claim is attributed in the source to Chapter 4 of Ding's book.
330160.analysis: Later primary theorem lists all eleven trinomials and proves their punctured value sets are Singer difference sets for every odd m>=5. 330175.title: Kano and Suzuki's colorful simplex partition conjecture
330175.statement:
Let $r \ge d\ge 3$ and $n\ge 1$ be integers. Let $X_1, X_2, \dots, X_r$ be $r$ disjoint point sets in $\mathbb{R}^d$. Assume that no $d+1$ points of $X_1 \cup X_2 \cup \dots \cup X_r$ lie in a hyperplane,

$$
\sum_{i=1}^r |X_i|=dn,
$$

and $|X_i| \le n$ for every $i\in [r]$. **Kano and Suzuki's colorful simplex partition conjecture.** There exist $n$ pairwise disjoint $(d-1)$-dimensional simplices, each of them having $d$ vertices in $d$ distinct sets $X_i$. This conjecture generalizes colorful simplex partitions and properly colored geometric matchings; the statement asks for a partition of all points into disjoint colorful simplices under the stated general-position and color-class-size conditions. Its resolution status is not established by the supplied source context.

330178.title: The 0-sum 3-flow conjecture for 2-edge-connected 5-regular graphs
330178.statement:
Let $G$ be a $2$-edge connected $5$-regular graph. A **$0$-sum $3$-flow** is a nowhere-zero flow whose values lie in $\{-2,-1,1,2\}$ and whose sum at every vertex is zero.

**0-sum 3-flow conjecture.** Every $2$-edge connected $5$-regular graph admits a $0$-sum $3$-flow.

The preceding theorem establishes the analogous assertion for every odd integer $r\geq 3$ with $r\neq 5$, leaving the $5$-regular case as the exceptional case addressed by this conjecture.
330178.analysis: Unsigned incident sums, not oriented conservation. Source proves the odd-regular cases other than degree 5. Backtracking labels 200 sampled 5-regular graphs (180 distinct labelled graphs) on even orders 6..24 using {-2,-1,1,2}; independent verification confirms every vertex sum zero, degree 5 and 2-edge-connectivity. No obstruction found.
330178.remaining_gap: Need uniform structural decomposition or a 2-edge-connected 5-regular graph with a certified unsatisfiable edge-labeling problem. Samples do not establish the conjecture.

330268.title: Existence conjecture for edge-colour complements of transversal graphs
330268.statement: Let $m\geqslant 0$ and let $\mathbb{R}_{m,m}$ be the real representation of the Clifford algebra. A **transversal graph** is an induced complete subgraph on $2^m$ vertices whose edges represent pairs of basis matrices with disjoint support; the edges are coloured by amicability and anti-amicability. **Transversal-graph colour-complement existence conjecture.** If a graph $T$ exists among the transversal graphs, then there exists at least one graph whose edge colours are complementary to those of $T$. This asserts existence of a colour-complementary transversal graph for every existing transversal graph; no resolution is given in the supplied material.
330268.analysis: The cited source itself disproves its Conjecture 3 for m>=4. A blue clique of order 2^m is a transversal; Hurwitz-Radon bounds red clique order by rho(2^m)<2^m, so no color-complementary transversal exists. Recreating that witness or its parameter instances earns zero.

330331.title: Shearer's conjecture on properly colored copies of graphs with few cherries
330331.statement:
Let $s$ and $k$ be integers. A coloring $c$ of $E(K_n)$ is **locally $k$-bounded** if no color appears more than $k$ times on the edges incident to any vertex. A graph $G$ is $G$-proper under $c$ if some copy of $G$ in $K_n$ has a proper edge-coloring induced by $c$.

**Shearer's conjecture.** For every two integers $s$ and $k$, there exists an integer $n_0$ such that, if $n\ge n_0$ and $G$ is an $n$-vertex graph with at most $sn$ cherries, then any locally $k$-bounded coloring of $E(K_n)$ is $G$-proper.

This generalizes the Bollobás–Erdős conjecture on properly colored Hamilton cycles to graphs with linearly many cherries. The source does not state whether this formulation has been resolved.
330331.analysis: The source explicitly proves Shearer in a stronger form: n-vertex graphs with r cherries embed properly into locally n/(560 r^(3/4))-bounded colorings. For r<=sn and fixed k the permitted bound grows with n. This is the source resolution, not a new corollary for campaign credit.
